method: Deterministic synthetic role-local ABA fixture. A stale writer observes visible_version=7, anchor_label=cross_field, generation=12 and a payload. The object is deleted and recreated with the same visible_version, same anchor_label and byte-identical payload but generation=13. Four CAS identities are compared: version+anchor label; version+anchor+monotone generation; version+anchor+payload hash; version+anchor+lineage hash bound to generation plus immutable creation parent.

candidate_comparison.success: rejects stale write in tested sequence
fails when recreated payload is byte-identical
rejects stale write in tested sequence
candidate_comparison.conflict_risk: low only if creation lineage input is itself non-reused
candidate_comparison.integration_cost: medium: bind identity to monotone generation or immutable non-reused parent

candidate_revision: Nominal anchor labels do not fix ABA if the label itself can repeat. A plain payload content hash also does not fix ABA when delete/recreate restores identical bytes. The tested sufficient guards are either a durable monotone generation that cannot rewind/reuse, or a lineage identity whose preimage includes a non-reused creation-generation/immutable-parent anchor. Therefore 'content-addressed' is safe here only when it addresses non-reused lineage, not payload alone.
tested_scope: Synthetic role-local single mutable-pointer object; one stale append writer; delete followed by recreation; deliberate reuse of visible version token and nominal anchor label; recreated payload deliberately byte-identical; monotone generation differs; lineage hash includes generation and immutable creation-parent label. No live Git transport/API atomicity, immutable checkpoint deletion, generation rollback/wraparound, forged or reused immutable parent, hash collision, more than two writers, multi-object transaction, retry after rejection, network partition, adversarial repository history rewrite or physical scheduler semantics were tested.

phase1_constraints.quota_zero_operation: The tested guard is local deterministic state logic and requires no hosted runner, Codespaces, artifacts/LFS/packages, cloud/API credits or external model execution.

Semantic input after freeze was only own r195 LATEST plus this deterministic synthetic role-local fixture. No O/O-derived state, other-worker state, downstream state, legacy research, aggregate ledger or other-role receipts/configs were consumed.
frontier: Test generation rollback/wraparound or restored-backup reuse as a separate child: determine whether monotonicity must be globally durable across restore and namespace reset.

Test lineage-parent reuse/forgery separately: if an immutable parent identity can be recreated or forged, determine whether a cryptographically collision-resistant content identity plus non-reused generation is necessary.
Only after those guards, consider multi-object atomicity or live Git transport as separate children if still highest-value.
exact_continuation: Next invocation bootstrap latest manifest/RUN_LIFECYCLE and freeze DESIRED_STATE plus cross_field config, reconstruct r196 from LATEST, then execute exactly one bounded child: simulate generation rollback/wraparound or backup-restore reuse where visible version, anchor label and generation can all repeat; test whether a non-reused immutable parent/lineage identity still rejects the stale writer and record the minimum invariant required. Do not start lineage forgery, live Git transport, multi-object atomicity, network-partition testing or a second leaf.
